deals.evidence: Wolves have been taken over for £45m by a Chinese group, Fosun International, the club has announced.
deals.headline: Fosun buys Wolves from Steve Morgan for £45m
deals.summary: Fosun International took 100% of Wolves from Steve Morgan's Bridgemere Group, committing £20-30m of investment over two years; the club said the terms were confidential, the Guardian reported £45m.

deals.evidence: US finance and technology firm PEAK6 Investments has acquired a minority share in Fosun Sports, the holding entity that operates Wolves
deals.headline: PEAK6 Investments buys a minority share in Fosun Sports, Wolves' holding entity
deals.summary: Chicago-based PEAK6 acquired an undisclosed minority share in Fosun Sports, the holding entity that operates Wolves, as a North American strategic partner.

deals.evidence: Fosun Sports Group are said to have bought back the shares sold to Peak6 three years ago, for a sum in the region of £39m.
deals.headline: Fosun buys back PEAK6's minority stake in Wolves' holding company (reported c.£39m)
deals.summary: Fosun Sports was reported to have bought back the minority shares sold to PEAK6 in 2021, for a sum reported in the region of £39m (around $50m); figure is reported, not confirmed by the club.

deals.evidence: Textor has submitted an offer of US$200 million in cash and US$350 million in shares in Eagle Football Holdings to Chinese conglomerate Fosun Group
deals.headline: John Textor's reported £400m approach for Wolves comes to nothing
deals.summary: Textor reportedly offered $200m in cash plus $350m in Eagle Football Holdings shares; Fosun was reported to want only a minority sale and the approach did not proceed.

notes: Wolves were relegated from the Premier League in April 2026 (BBC) and play in the Championship in 2026/27; the league field keeps the batch's value. Financial year 2024/25 was extended to 13 months ending 30 June 2025: revenue £172.0m; the release gives the loss after interest and tax (£15.3m) but no pre-tax, operating, wage, net-debt or revenue-split figures, and the full accounts PDF is a scanned image. Companies House: W.W. (1990) Limited (02487393) is the club company's 75%+ PSC; its PSC is Guo Guangchang (50-75%, as a member of a firm). The 100% stake is the 2016 transfer; PEAK6's 2021 minority was at the Fosun Sports holding level and was bought back (reported). No Forbes team page or valuation found; Molineux capacity is only stated as 'more than 30,000' on the club's events site, so left null; stadium ownership not stated on a citable page. Chief executive: not found on a citable page; Nathan Shi (executive chairman since May 2026, interim from December 2025) runs day-to-day operations. Old record had revenue only; source kept.

owners.evidence: the transfer of the 100% ownership in Wolves and all its assets from Steve Morgan CBE and his Bridgemere Group to Fosun Group (Fosun) headed by Chairman Guo Guangchang
owners.name: Fosun International (Fosun Sports)

ownership_summary: Wolves have been owned since July 2016 by China's Fosun Group, which bought 100% of the club from Steve Morgan's Bridgemere Group; the club company's parent is W.W. (1990) Limited, whose registered person with significant control is Fosun chairman Guo Guangchang. The holding entity Fosun Sports sold a minority share to PEAK6 Investments in 2021 and bought it back in 2024; Fosun rejected or did not take up John Textor's reported £400m approach in October 2025.
revenue_evidence: Revenue for the period totalled £172.0m (£177.7m in 2023/24)
revenue_source_name: Wolves headline financial information for 2024/25 (13 months to 30 June 2025)
